interest: Shows Japanese anti-Soviet propaganda in neutral Afghanistan, and Kabul's push to replace Japanese engineers with American ones.
overview: Docket (1942-44) on Japanese activity in Afghanistan: anti-Soviet propaganda, Japanese irrigation engineers, and Afghan students' reports on wartime Japan.

people.name: Senji Kobayashi
people.role: Japanese engineer employed on the irrigation canal at Jochra

people.name: Charles W. Thayer
people.role: U.S. Foreign Service Officer / Secretary of Legation in Kabul

subfiles.about: A two-page State Department list of papers cataloguing fifteen diplomatic communications and cross-references from 1942 to 1944 concerning alleged Japanese activities, propaganda, engineers, and students in Afghanistan.
subfiles.summary: Lists fifteen 1942-44 items: Japanese anti-Soviet propaganda, irrigation engineers replaced by Americans, and Afghan students returning from Japan via Siberia.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Alleged Japanese activities in Afghanistan
